text: Business owners, doing nothing: the baseline.
Business owners pay each child up to $15,750 a year (within the reasonable cap for the age) while the business runs; each child puts what it can in a Roth IRA.
Business owners convert $100,000 of IRA to Roth every year until the IRAs are empty.
Business owners, the greedy search's best plan: children's wages and Roth IRAs, $100,000 conversions, children's gains realised up to their 0% band, a later wage, one annual-exclusion gift.
Early retirees, the greedy search's best plan: conversions sized by period, and charity given in shares.
High earners, doing nothing (their estate pays estate tax).
High earners give $500,000 of shares to the children at once.
High earners, the greedy search's best plan: the gift, conversions to the top of the 24% row, charity in shares.
Investors living on an $8 million portfolio, doing nothing.
Investors give their usual $30,000 a year to charity in appreciated shares instead of cash.
Investors, the greedy search's best plan: charity in shares, annual-exclusion gifts while the children are 15 to 18, conversions, the children's gains realised in their 0% band.
